history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE (DIGAMBARA SECT), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Shri 1008 Parshvanath Digambar Jain Mandir stands about 250 metres inside the Badshahpur main market off the Gurugram-Sohna road. It was constructed around 350 years ago by the local Jain community and renovated over time. The temple has three vedis (altars): the mulnayak in the mool vedi is Shri 1008 Parshvanath Bhagwan, consecrated in Vikram Samvat 1457 (1400 CE), alongside idols of Chandraprabhu, Neminath, Shantinath and Bahubali. The second and third vedis were built in 1987 by Phoolmati Jain (wife of Anoop Singh Jain); the second vedi's mulnayak is a very ancient Shri Neminath idol said to date to the 14th century. The garbh grah has glass paintings of Tirthankaras, and regular worship, abhishek and religious activities are performed by the local Jain community. IDENTITY NOTE: several 'Digambar Jain Temple' listings exist in Gurugram (Parsavsthali at Hans Enclave, NH-8 - est. 2006; one on Basai Road, Sector 11; the Kasangaon Atishay Kshetra off the Delhi-Jaipur highway). The Badshahpur shrine is documented here because it is the best-sourced ancient one; if the CSV intended a different listing, it needs correction.

town_description: Badshahpur is a town on the Gurugram-Sohna corridor in Gurugram district, Haryana, about 10-12 km south of old Gurgaon (verify). It grew around an old settlement near the historic Badshahpur fort and has now been absorbed into Gurugram's southern expansion along Sohna Road. The town is known for the ancient Parshvanath Digambar Jain Mandir in its main market and is close to the ISKCON Sri Sri Radha Damodar Mandir.
